_doc: Per-scope step membership for the `gz check` runner (GHI #950). A scope names the steps it DROPS, never the steps it keeps, so a newly registered step is IN every scope until someone deliberately excludes it -- the conservative polarity, matching `overlaps_writers` in data/check_step_concurrency.json. This file exists because the roster was a module-level frozenset in src/gzkit/commands/quality.py, which made 'which steps does the push gate actually run' a code question rather than a declared one. A scope missing from `scopes`, or a missing file, means NO skips: the runner falls back to the full sweep rather than silently dropping steps it could not read a policy for. `records_verified` is the load-bearing field -- a scope that drops any step is a PARTIAL verification, and letting a partial pass record the fingerprint the pre-push gate reuses is precisely the presence-check failure AGENTS.md names ('A PRESENCE CHECK ANSWERS is something armed, NEVER did the governed procedure run'). A scope may record only when it drops nothing the per-change gate runs: `change` (the default, and what the pre-push hook runs) and `full` record (GHI #1088). The `fast` scope was retired 2026-10-11 (GHI #1191), when the `change` scope took its shape: a scope that drops `Test` runs `Test (changed)` in its place. Since 2026-10-11 (GHI #1192, operator ruling, verbatim: 'adopters get the light gate too') this file ships inside the gzkit package and is read from there, never from the invoking project's data/, so every project that installs gzkit runs the same per-change gate.

change.rationale: AMENDED 2026-10-11 (GHI #1191, operator ruling, verbatim: 'I can live with fewer comprehensive checks for daily work with more quality runs at a lesser frequency. I think at minor or patch releases and also as a chore are good places for full qc runs.'): the per-change gate also drops `Test`, `Docs build` and `Guard canary sweep`, and runs `Test (changed)`, the tests the change touches, in place of `Test`. Measured that day on a 10-core host (a dated record): `Test` 117.25s in-gate against 16.34s wall for every remaining step together; the unit tier's wall time was set by one serial test, the 22-mutant canary kill sweep, which is now the full-tier step `Guard canary sweep`. The whole unit tier runs under `gz check --full`, which CI runs on every code push; at OBPI completion (Gate 2, `gz test`); at release (`gz patch release`); and in the `quality-check` chore. What is given up: because work lands on main, a unit failure the changed-test selection misses is reported by CI after the push, and a broken docs link likewise. The sentences below that say this scope keeps the unit tier are the record of 2026-09-24 and are superseded on that point. The DEFAULT scope of plain `gz check` and the scope the pre-push hook runs (GHI #1088). AGENTS.md § Gate Covenant binds the unit tier to every change and `behave` to heavy-lane OBPI work and CI, never to a per-change gate; `gz check --full` is the explicit full sweep, and CI runs it. Until GHI #1088 this was the `prepush` scope, reachable only through `--reuse-verified`, while plain `gz check` was the full sweep and the only scope that could record the reuse fingerprint, so an agent following AGENTS.md § Execution Rules paid Behave on every change to skip a push-gate run that would not have run Behave. It records because it drops nothing the gate that reuses the fingerprint would run. Behave (operator ruling 2026-09-02) is Heavy-lane / closeout-scope by src/gzkit/commands/sync.py's own ruling ('Behave no longer runs as a sync pre-gate ... behave is Heavy-lane / closeout-scope'), but that ruling was applied to git-sync's gate and never reached the `gz check` the pre-push hook calls, so it kept running on every push through the other door. Measured 2026-09-02: 30.61s, the single largest step in the sweep, against 29.10s for Test and 3.90s for Docs build. CI runs the full sweep including Behave (.github/workflows/ci.yml). Removing the step from `gz check` outright was rejected: `Behave` is a declared writer in data/check_step_concurrency.json and is named by test_check_step_writer_overlap.py, test_behave_sharding.py and test_check_step_concurrency.py, so deletion would ripple through the concurrency subsystem to buy the same seconds a scope entry buys here. Preflight (operator ruling 2026-09-02) is a JANITORIAL SCAN, not a correctness gate: it reports stale pipeline markers, orphan receipts and expired locks, and its own output says 'Run with --apply to clean up'. Its verdict is a function of WALL-CLOCK AGE, not of the content being pushed -- `find_stale_pipeline_markers` compares `updated_at` against STALE_MARKER_HOURS=4 -- so it can turn red with no edit at all, and it cannot distinguish a LIVE checkpoint from abandoned residue. Measured instance: OBPI-0.35.0-04 was checkpointed mid-flight with its lock held and `resume_point: verify`, and its two markers then failed Preflight on every commit, locally and in CI, regardless of what was being pushed. A cleanup to-do list must not refuse a push. The full sweep still runs it, so the hygiene signal is not lost -- it simply stops gating. AMENDED 2026-10-28 (RO-9 tranche 5, operator ruling, verbatim selection: 'Full tier only (Rec.)'): the per-change gate also drops `Supply chain audit`. `uv audit` needs the network, so an offline commit could not pass it, and its verdict moves with the advisory databases rather than with the change, the same ground on which `Preflight` was dropped. It runs under `gz check --full`: in CI on every code push, at release and in the quality-check chore.

cross-platform.rationale: GHI #1253 (operator ruling 2026-10-16, verbatim: 'fix #1253 now'). The scope the second CI platform runs: the full sweep minus the steps whose verdict cannot depend on the platform, because the Linux job of the same CI run already returns that verdict. Windows is in the CI matrix for one failure class (.github/workflows/ci.yml, the comment above `strategy:`): compared paths (#383), console encoding (#275), subprocess decoding (#582), line endings (#681), and a typecheck exclude glob that never matched (#788). Every step that reads repository paths, spawns a subprocess, decodes output or compares bytes reaches that class and stays, which is nearly all of them; the classification is per step, and a step not named here runs. Dropped: `Guard canary sweep`, which grades whether each guard's designated test kills its mutant, a property of test logic; its copy-and-mutate machinery is exercised on Windows by tests/governance/test_guard_canaries.py inside `Test`. `Preflight`, whose verdict is a function of wall-clock age (see the `change` rationale). Measured 2026-10-16 on CI run 38875151441 (a dated record): the sweep took 280.51s on windows-latest and runs after `Test` finishes, so it sat directly on the critical path (Test 787s + sweep 280s against a 1085s gate step). Kept although free of the class, because dropping it frees no wall time: `Docs build` runs in the writer lane, which `Test` overlaps. Never records: it drops nothing the per-change gate runs, but RECORDABLE_SCOPES carries only `change` and `full`, and CI never reuses a fingerprint. AMENDED 2026-10-28 (RO-9 tranche 5): `Supply chain audit` is dropped too. It audits the one lock against one service, a verdict no platform changes, and the Linux job of the same run returns it.
